newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica cabinet approves controversial labour bill.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica cabinet approves controversial labour bill.

text.p: South Africa's Labour Minister Tito Mboweni on Thursday unveiled a controversial new employment bill which has threatened to become a flashpoint between trade unions and business.

Tito Mboweni told reporters the cabinet had approved the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill which would now go for discussion to the tri-partite National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac).
The bill should be tabled during the current session of parliament if government, business and labour can reach agreement within Nedlac, he said.
"The bill is the united position of cabinet in line with its commitment to reconstruction and development," Mboweni said.
"The total package is an attractive one for South Africa but the details will be in the negotiations," he added.
Industry leaders fear the new legislation will raise their costs while labour is concerned that proposals designed to protect workers may be watered down.
In line with the Green Paper released in February last year, the bill retains proposals to reduce weekly working hours to 45 from 46 hours, including mine, farm and shift workers.
It proposes a large reduction in working hours for security workers from 60 hours a week to 45 hours.

The bill, which for the first time also includes public service employees, also proposes an increase in overtime pay from time-and-a-third to time-and-a-half -- a proposal that employers strongly oppose.
The bill also proposes four months maternity leave instead of the present 12 weeks and double pay for workers who work on Sundays.
The present Employment Act, which the bill will replace, violates international standards on maternity leave as well as clauses in the new South African constitution, officials said.
